q1: SELECT beer, MAX(price) - MIN(price) AS price_gap, AVG(price) AS avg_price FROM serves WHERE beer IN (SELECT s.beer FROM serves AS s, frequents AS f WHERE s.bar = f.bar AND f.drinker LIKE 'B%' GROUP BY s.beer HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s.bar) >= 2) GROUP BY beer ORDER BY beer

explanation: Q1 filters beers by counting distinct bars from the join with frequents where drinker LIKE 'B%' and HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT bar) >= 2. Q2 counts distinct bars from the entire serves table (not just those linked to B% drinkers) after including beers from BeersByBDrinker. If a beer is served in one bar frequented by a B% drinker and another bar not frequented by any B% drinker, Q1 counts 1 bar (excluded), while Q2 counts 2 bars (included).
counterexample_dsp: A beer served in two bars: one frequented by a B% drinker and one not. Q1 excludes the beer due to insufficient bars linked to B% drinkers, while Q2 includes it because it counts all bars from serves.
